titles.title: FarCry
titles.engine: CryEngine 1 - Far Cry 1.4 (GOG 2.0.0.9, FileVersion 1.4.0.1405), Direct3D9 renderer Bin32\XRenderD3D9.dll
titles.launch_sets: 1920x1080x32 fullscreen on the 1080p LCDs, from a mechanism that is present and correct. 'Play Far Cry.bat' copies System-fleet.cfg over System.cfg, calls FLEETRES.BAT, then runs FLEETRES -setline System.cfg r_Width/r_Height = `%FR_W%`/`%FR_H%` (the backticks become the quotes the engine requires). agent/shared/gameres.h:773-774 write the same values at GAMESYNC. Measured on .145: log.txt reads 'Lua cvar: (r_Width,1920)', 'Best-match display mode: 1920x1080x32 (Error=8)' and 'Current Resolution: 1920x1080x32 Full Screen'. Real 1920x1080 main-menu frames exist for .123 and .246 (now .195); I viewed both. Caveat for .240: FLEETRES needs the EDID at launch time. .240 read no EDID after its 23:40 reboot, but did read it again (DELL E2313H, 1920x1080 in the mode list) at 00:35 in my read-only FLEETRES -info run.
titles.menu_source: The list comes from the driver. The Options > Video 'Resolution' combo (FCData/Scripts.pak SCRIPTS/MenuScreens/Options/Video.lua, widget_resolution.user.Initialize, lines 617-641) is filled from System:EnumDisplayFormats(). Its only filter is `DispFmt.bpp == 32 and DispFmt.width > 640 and DispFmt.height > 480`, and entries are added as 'WxHx32'. XRenderD3D9's EnumDisplayFormats (0x3806cef2) copies every entry of the adapter mode list at [adapter+0x458], mapping 24 bpp to 32, with no size or aspect filter. The renderer's own best-match search (0x38011466-0x38011540) walks that same +0x458 list. On .145 it found an exact 1920x1080 entry: Error=8 is only the bpp term, because the search counts X8R8G8B8 as 24 bits.
titles.evidence: Surveyor's: Play Far Cry.bat and System-fleet.cfg in /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/FarCry/; gameres.h:773-774; .claude/evidence-1080p/g6-farcry-bf1942-maxpayne-redfaction-tribes2-r6/{farcry_enumdisplayformats_disasm.txt, 145_FarCry_log.txt, 145_FarCry_System.cfg, perbox-2026-08-31_123_FarCry_Play_Far_Cry.png, perbox-2026-08-31_246_FarCry_Play_Far_Cry.png, gameres_*_2026-09-29.json}. Reviewer: re-extracted Video.lua from Scripts.pak and read lines 617-661; disassembled the XRenderD3D9.dll best-match loop; viewed both perbox frames (real 1920x1080 menus, not desktops). The .240 EDID read-back is in .claude/evidence-1080p/review-g6/fleetres_info_cap1024x768_240.txt.
titles.fix_source: already in tree (Play Far Cry.bat + FLEETRES.EXE/.BAT + System-fleet.cfg; gameres.h rules 773-774)
titles.fix_risk: None for the menu. By design the launcher resets System.cfg at every start, so a mode picked in the menu lasts one session only. Native TCP/IP multiplayer does not depend on resolution.
titles.hw_check: Do this on .145 or .123 (XP, where GDI captures fullscreen D3D), and only when no other session is using the box. EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\FarCry" "Play Far Cry.bat", wait about 60 s, then SCREENSHOT 0 should show the 1920x1080 main menu. DOWNLOAD C:\Games\FarCry\log.txt and look for 'Current Resolution: 1920x1080x32 Full Screen'. Menu path: Options > Video > Resolution combo; expect a '1920x1080x32' entry. Navigation: the compat DB records that 'CryEngine takes DirectInput exclusively', so absolute UICLICK is not expected to land. Tab/Enter is plausible (the widgets have tabstops) but unproven. Keyboard-only alternative: UIKEY TILDE, then UIKEY TEXT:#for i,f in System:EnumDisplayFormats() do System:Log(f.width.."x"..f.height.."x"..f.bpp) end, then UIKEY RETURN, quit, and DOWNLOAD log.txt. The '#' Lua console prefix is engine knowledge, not verified. On .195 rely on log.txt rather than a screenshot. On .240, first run FLEETRES -info to confirm it reads the EDID.
titles.verifier_notes: confirmed. I re-derived the menu filter from Video.lua myself. I also checked that the renderer's best-match search walks the same +0x458 list that EnumDisplayFormats copies, so the logged exact 1920x1080 hit ties the menu's source list to the panel mode. It is still not observed on screen. I did not launch it because every LCD box was running another session's test at review time: CARMA2_HW.EXE on .123 (live mode 640x480), sof2mp_t1080.exe on .240, quake3.exe on .195, and .145 between Quake 3 runs. A fullscreen launch would have broken their captures. Added the .240 EDID caveat.

titles.title: BF1942
titles.engine: Refractor 1 - Battlefield 1942 v1.61b (BF1942.exe md5 a56d63e83eb5e02b43e1928cb22cd15a, PE 2004-10-19, D3D8), rebuilt from EA 1.6.19 + 1.61b; SafeDisc 2.80.010 on Mods\bf1942\Mod.dll
titles.launch_sets: The launchers write 1920x1080, but the client never runs on this fleet. 'Play Battlefield 1942.bat' (lines 54-59, generated from provisioning/discmount/specs/BF1942.json fleetres_block) and 'Join Battlefield 1942 - LAN.bat' (lines 27-32) run FLEETRES -setline 'game.setGameDisplayMode %FR_W% %FR_H% 32 0' into Profiles\Default\Video.con and Profiles\Custom\Video.con. gameres.h:770-771 do the same at sync; .145's files read 1920 1080 32 0. The engine would accept the mode: the renderer list at +0xa8 is NOT the raw adapter list, as the surveyor said. It is D3D8 EnumAdapterModes filtered by 0x63fc70: 640x480@60 and 800x600@60 are always kept, and anything else only if (w,h,refresh,bpp) matches the GDI EnumDisplaySettings list built at 0x640470 (16/32 bpp, non-interlaced, 60 Hz only when a flag argument is set). There is no aspect filter, and GDI lists 1920x1080@60x32 on all four LCD boxes, so setVideoMode's exact match (0x63dc40) would succeed. Two gaps in the writers. (1) Only the Default and Custom profiles are rewritten. A profile created in-game is seeded (0x4435f3...) with copies of Settings\Default\VideoLow/Medium/High.con (800x600) as its Video.con and VideoCustom.con and is never corrected. (2) The Join launcher starts the client without mounting the disc, so it fails the EA disc-GUID check as well as SafeDisc. Only the Host shortcut (a console dedicated server with no display mode) runs. SafeDisc 2.80.010 raises 'Cannot locate the CD-ROM' with the image correctly mounted (compat DB: .124, .133, .143, .240, .246).
titles.menu_source: The driver list passes through a hardcoded aspect filter. The Video page's 'DisplayModeList' widget (created at 0x6b04b1) is filled at 0x6b0833-0x6b09e6. A mode is listed only if 0x45f8d0 returns true (w == 4*h, the TripleHead 4:1 test) or (float)h/(float)w == 0.75 exactly (the double at 0x8dbfa0, which I read as 0.75; `test ah,44h / jp skip`), and also w >= 640 and h >= 480. Entries are formatted '%dx%dx%d @ %d' or '%dx%dx%d'. 1920x1080 (0.5625) and 1280x1024 (0.8) are never listed.
titles.evidence: Surveyor's: .claude/evidence-1080p/g6-farcry-bf1942-maxpayne-redfaction-tribes2-r6/{bf1942_options_video_4x3_filter_disasm.txt, 145_BF1942_Profiles_*_Video.con}. Reviewer: .claude/evidence-1080p/review-g6/bf1942_reviewer_disasm.txt covers the filter, the file bytes at 0x2b08d0 ('75 37' at 0x2b08d6), the renderer predicate 0x63fc70 with the GDI list 0x640470, profile seeding 0x4435f3, and the Custom-level VideoCustom.con load at 0x6b171f. Staged files are under /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/BF1942/Mods/bf1942/Settings/: Default/VideoLow|Medium|High|VideoCustom.con and Profiles/Default|Custom/VideoCustom.con all say 800 600. Compat DB compat_render rows for BF1942 on .124/.133/.143/.240/.246 record 'Cannot locate the CD-ROM' with the disc mounted.
titles.fix: The in-game list cannot show 1080p without patching EA's exe. One byte in BF1942.exe at file offset 0x2b08d6 (VA 0x6b08d6): 0x75 becomes 0xEB, turning `jne 0x6b090f` into `jmp`, so every renderer mode of at least 640x480 is listed. I verified the bytes are 75 37. The preset handling needs more than the surveyor listed. Rewrite the mode line per box; do NOT delete it, because the menu parses nine values out of each preset (0x6af953) and a missing line may leave the mode field empty. The line must be rewritten in Settings\Default\VideoLow.con, VideoMedium.con, VideoHigh.con AND VideoCustom.con, and in every Settings\Profiles\*\Video.con and VideoCustom.con (or the active profile named in Settings\Profile.con), not only Default/Custom Video.con. The Custom performance level loads <profile>\VideoCustom.con (0x6b171f), and new profiles copy the presets. Where to change it: BF1942.json fleetres_block (the Play launcher is a generated mount launcher; regenerate it with make-mount-launcher.py), the hand-written Join launcher, stage-fleetres.py, and gameres.h:770-771 (keep them mirrored). None of this can be tested until the SafeDisc 2.80.010 client wall is solved: the pressed disc, or a mounter that emulates 2.80.
titles.fix_source: The byte patch is made by hand. Nothing on the share fixes the menu (case-insensitive search of Game Updates, Patches, Games\Mods & Patches, Games\Windows XP, GOG, Inbox, Installed, _preserved-from-fleet, Utility, tmp, tmp_install). 'Game Updates' holds only bf1942-patch-1.6.19-full.exe and bf1942-1.6-to-1.61b.exe. tmp_install\Battlefield.1942.7z and Games\_preserved-from-fleet\Battlefield.1942 are the djDEVASTATE scene repack: 1.6 exe plus the 4 KB crack-stub Mod.dll that README-FLEET deliberately stripped. Not usable. The preset edits are to files already in the tree.
titles.fix_risk: The byte patch changes the md5 of EA's own BF1942.exe, which breaks README-FLEET's 'every executable is EA's own' promise. Never combine it with the stripped no-CD stub. A PunkBuster-enabled Internet server would kick a modified exe; the LAN dedicated server does not check client binaries. Deleting (rather than rewriting) preset mode lines risks an empty or invalid mode ('Invalid videomode specified'). A per-box rewrite of preset files that the engine also copies means GAMESYNC will see them as changed. 16:9 at the staged renderer.fieldOfView 1 may look wrong (unverified).
titles.hw_check: This is impossible today on every box: the Play and Join clients both stop at SafeDisc, and Join does not even mount the disc. Once a client can start: DOWNLOAD Profiles\Default\Video.con and Profiles\Custom\Video.con after the launcher runs (both should read 1920 1080 32 0). On XP, SCREENSHOT the main menu, which should be 1920x1080. Then open Options > Video and screenshot the display-mode list. BF1942 draws its own cursor and keyboard navigation is not established, so if absolute clicks do not land it needs a human once.
titles.verifier_notes: Menu verdict and patch bytes confirmed. Corrected the renderer claim: its mode list is D3D8 modes intersected with EnumDisplaySettings (with 640x480@60 and 800x600@60 always kept), not the full adapter list. The conclusion that 1920x1080x32 is accepted still holds. Widened the preset fix to the three VideoCustom.con files and to profiles created in-game (seeded from the presets), and advised rewriting rather than deleting lines. Noted that the Play launcher must be changed through its discmount spec, and that the Join launcher runs the SafeDisc client without mounting. So CLAUDE.md's 'LAN launchers check neither disc nor CD key' is true only of Host. Added the share-search result: the only other BF1942 copies are the cracked repack.

titles.title: MaxPayne
titles.engine: MAX-FX - Max Payne retail v1.05 (in-exe stamp 'Thu Jan 17 09:49:00 2002'), D3D8 via e2driver\e2_d3d8_driver_mfc.dll; SafeDisc 2.51.020
titles.launch_sets: 1920x1080x32, set in the registry, and correct in the staged tree. 'Play Max Payne.bat' (generated from provisioning/discmount/specs/MaxPayne.json) calls FLEETRES and then -reg HKCU 'Software\Remedy Entertainment\Max Payne\Video Settings' Display Width=%FR_W% and Display Height=%FR_H%. It then starts MaxPayne.exe -nodialog -skipstartup. gameres.h:751-752 write the same values after install.reg, which pins 800x600x32. Read back 2026-09-29 on .123, .145, .195 and .240: 1920/1080/32. The route is proven: .133 rendered in-game at FLEETRES's 1280x960 (compat DB, manual row). It has never been seen rendering on a 1080p LCD. The .246 'verified 1920x1080' row is a desktop-only frame (I viewed it). The .240 'failed' row predates the -nodialog fix. .123 was 'n/a' when it had no mounter, and .145 is untested. Launching also needs SafeDisc 2.51.020 satisfied, which means DAEMON Tools 3.47 with Emulation > SafeDisc on. .123 and .145 report d347bus, but the emulation state is unknown. .195 has only WinCDEmu, which emulates nothing, so .195 is probably unlaunchable.
titles.menu_source: There is no in-game resolution option. The in-game VIDEO page is exactly GCID_TEXTUREMIPMAP 'Texture Sharpness' and GCID_GAMMACONTROL 'Brightness' (plaintext #defines in x_english.ras). Resolution exists only in the pre-game CMaxPayneStartupDialog (Display Adapter / Screen Mode / Acceleration), inside MaxPayne.exe. Its Screen Mode list comes from the driver: it keeps every mode with w>=640 and h>=480 (0x406bd7-0x406c9e, read from the SafeDisc-stripped copy of the same build). The retail e2_d3d8_driver_mfc.dll drops a mode only if IDirect3D8::CheckDeviceType (vtbl+0x24) or CheckDeviceFormat (+0x28) fails, before linkMode; there is no size or aspect test. That dialog would therefore list 1920x1080x32, but the fleet passes -nodialog, so players never see it.
titles.evidence: Surveyor's: Play Max Payne.bat, install.reg and README-FLEET.txt under /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/MaxPayne/; gameres.h:751-752; .claude/evidence-1080p/g6-farcry-bf1942-maxpayne-redfaction-tribes2-r6/{maxpayne_startup_dialog_modes_disasm.txt, registry_readback_lcd_boxes.json, perbox-2026-08-31_246_MaxPayne_Play_Max_Payne.png}. Reviewer: .claude/evidence-1080p/review-g6/maxpayne_reviewer_notes.txt covers the x_english.ras VIDEO defines, the retail driver filter, the Fixes-zip PE subsystems, and the byte diff of the Fixes-zip e2 DLLs against retail. Compat DB compat_render rows: .133 manual in-game 1280x960; .240 pre-fix 'no GAME process after 90s'.
titles.fix: No fix is needed for 1080p: the per-box HKCU mode is already 1920x1080x32 on the LCD boxes, and no in-game selector exists to fix. If a visible selector is wanted, add a second shortcut through the same mount template with GAMEARGS='-skipstartup' (no -nodialog). That exposes the dialog's driver-enumerated Screen Mode list; the next 'Play' launch re-asserts the panel mode. That shortcut must be labelled as opening a dialog and kept out of automated per-box sweeps. The spec's own note records that exactly this idle dialog was mis-recorded as 'no GAME process after 90s' on three boxes. Do not stage anything from Max_Payne_Fixes.zip. Its MaxPayne.exe is a no-CD crack; d3d8.dll (Ultimate ASI Loader) and MaxPayne.WidescreenFix.asi are PE subsystem 6.0, which XP refuses; dsound.dll is IndirectSound. Separately, correct README-FLEET: its claim that the zip's e2mfc.dll and e2_d3d8_driver_mfc.dll 'unlock extra resolutions' is wrong. The diff shows only a DllMain run-once guard and a plugin entry-point call.
titles.fix_source: Already in the tree. The optional shortcut goes through provisioning/discmount/specs/MaxPayne.json + scripts/fleet/make-mount-launcher.py + launch.txt. A 16:9 HUD/FOV would need ThirteenAG's WidescreenFix, which is in the zip but works on .195 (Win7) only.
titles.fix_risk: Low. Single player only, so there is no multiplayer or anti-cheat impact. At 16:9 without ThirteenAG's fix the 4:3 image is likely stretched (unverified). A dialog-first shortcut looks like a hang to process-presence automation. On the label: the surveyor's 'probe never matches, remounts every launch' is not established. The generator spec keeps VOLID=MAX_PAYNE on purpose (its _note says 'Max Payne' was the wrong one), while README-FLEET says the reverse. The MARKER fallback (maxpayne.ico) catches the mounted disc either way.
titles.hw_check: On .145 (XP, DAEMON Tools), when idle: confirm tray > Emulation > SafeDisc is ticked (screenshot the right-click tray menu). Then EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\MaxPayne" "Play Max Payne.bat" and after about 45 s SCREENSHOT 0 should show the main menu at 1920x1080 (XP captures D3D8 fullscreen). REGREAD HKCU Software\Remedy Entertainment\Max Payne\Video Settings should read 1920/1080/32. To see the selector, start MaxPayne.exe with the disc mounted and without -nodialog. The startup dialog is an ordinary Win32 MFC dialog, so the keyboard (Alt+S for Screen Mode, then the arrow keys) and UICLICK both work; screenshot the open combo and look for '1920 x 1080 x 32'. On .240, first confirm FLEETRES -info reads the EDID.
titles.verifier_notes: Core findings confirmed: the no-menu verdict, the driver-enumerated dialog, the HKCU mechanism, and that the .246 row is a desktop-only frame (I viewed it). Corrections: (1) the VOLID/remount remark is contradicted by the generator spec, and the MARKER fallback makes the probe work, so the remount is not established; (2) README-FLEET's 'unlock extra resolutions' claim about the Fixes-zip e2 DLLs is false by byte diff, which supports the surveyor's reading; (3) added the automation hazard of a dialog-first shortcut; (4) .195 cannot pass SafeDisc with WinCDEmu, so a 1080p proof must come from .145 or .123.

titles.title: RedFaction
titles.engine: Geo-Mod - Red Faction build 177 (build.ver 0xB1; install.reg says v1.20; rf.exe md5 0ba3b15d64a702333a4d9a0815f782b7, linked 2001-09-03; Direct3D 8 at run time)
titles.launch_sets: 640x480 on every box today, because the mechanism writes the WRONG HIVE. The launcher's FLEETRES block (lines 55-58, copied from provisioning/discmount/specs/RedFaction.json fleetres_block) and gameres.h:753-755 write HKLM\SOFTWARE\Volition\Red Faction. rf.exe registers 'Resolution Width/Height/Bit Depth' with a NULL section (0x4b1480; defaults 0x280/0x1e0/0x10). For a NULL section, 0x52b2a0 returns HKCU (ebp=0x80000001) plus the base path built at 0x52b570: 'Software\' + 'Volition' + '\' + 'Red Faction'. Only a section string starting 'hkey' selects another root, and there is no HKLM fallback. Registry state agrees: HKLM holds 1920/1080/32 on .123/.145/.195/.240, and HKCU holds only install.reg's UpdateRate etc. The tree's own README-FLEET found the same trap for networking ('There is NO ConnectionSpeed value under HKLM ... does nothing at all'). Frames: 640x480 menus on .246 and .133; the .143 '1024x768 verified' row is a desktop-only frame (I viewed it).
titles.menu_source: rf.exe has no reachable in-game screen-resolution option. Both halves of its vestigial selector are dead code: the setter 0x4b15d0 (table at 0x5a1298 = {640x480, 800x600, 1024x768, 1280x1024}) and the index getter 0x4b1650 have no call, jmp or imm32 reference anywhere. The only resolution UI is the separate vendor launcher RedFaction.exe (Setup > Video > Detect Available Cards). It keeps a D3D8 mode only if it equals its hardcoded table at 0x4ad5d0 = {640x480, 800x600, 1024x768, 1280x1024} (loop 0x401187), so 1920x1080 can never appear. The fleet launcher bypasses it and starts rf.exe directly.
titles.evidence: Surveyor's: .claude/evidence-1080p/g6-farcry-bf1942-maxpayne-redfaction-tribes2-r6/{redfaction_rf_exe_reads_HKCU_disasm.txt, registry_readback_lcd_boxes.json, perbox-2026-08-31_246/133/143_RedFaction_*.png}. Reviewer: .claude/evidence-1080p/review-g6/redfaction_reviewer_disasm.txt covers the root and base-path build, the dead getter/setter xrefs, the HUD selector and its callers, the BSS placement, the strings.tbl artifact, the launcher table, and the version-string note. Also /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/RedFaction/install.reg and README-FLEET.txt (HKCU for per-user settings), provisioning/discmount/specs/RedFaction.json, and Dash Faction's README (github.com/rafalh/dashfaction: 'Windows 7 and newer', 1.20 NA only).
titles.fix: (1) Move the write to HKCU in all THREE places. First, provisioning/discmount/specs/RedFaction.json fleetres_block, then regenerate 'Play Red Faction.bat' with make-mount-launcher.py. The shipped launcher is a generated mount launcher, and stage-fleetres.py skips any launcher that already calls FLEETRES, so editing only stage-fleetres.py (as the surveyor proposed) changes nothing on the share. Second, the RedFaction entry in scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py (tests read it). Third, gameres.h:753-755 (root "HKCU", same value names, DWORD). Optionally delete the stray HKLM values, and update PER-TITLE-STATUS.md. (2) Choose the mode knowing that the HUD block selector 0x4377f0 is keyed on WIDTH ONLY. Widths 640, 800, 1024 and 1280 load a hud.tbl block. Any other width leaves 0x637628 as zero BSS, so every HUD element would sit at (0,0) (inferred). Width 1280 loads the #1280x1024 block even at 1280x960, the 4:3 target FLEETRES gives the LCD boxes, which would put bottom HUD elements about 64 px off-screen (inferred). The only HUD-safe modes are exactly 640x480, 800x600, 1024x768 and 1280x1024. Test 1920x1080 on one box first. If the HUD is broken, clamp in the batch file (FR_W43/FR_H43, set to 1024x768 when FR_W43 > 1024) and record Red Faction as capped 4:3. Do NOT use FLEETRES -cap 1024 768: on .123 and .240 it re-targets to 848x480 and yields FR_W43 = 640x480. (3) A true 16:9 HUD/FOV needs Dash Faction, which is Windows 7+ and 1.20 NA only per its README, and is not on the share. dgVoodoo 2.87, which IS on the share, could force a higher internal render resolution for this D3D8 game on .195 only, while rf.exe keeps a HUD-safe 1024x768. That is untested and still 4:3. A 1080p entry in any Red Faction menu is impossible on stock rf.exe.
titles.fix_source: The FLEETRES.EXE already staged here (its -reg option supports HKCU) plus edits to provisioning/discmount/specs/RedFaction.json, scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py and agent/shared/gameres.h. Dash Faction would have to be downloaded from github.com/rafalh/dashfaction releases; it is not on the share (case-insensitive search). dgVoodoo 2.87 is at \\192.168.1.122\files\Files\Game Updates\dgVoodoo2_87.zip; its x86 DDraw/D3DImm/D3D8/D3D9 DLLs are subsystem 6.0, so it runs on .195 only.
titles.fix_risk: The hive change itself is low risk; the HUD at non-table widths is the real risk, so test on one box before pushing fleet-wide. Several tests must move together: test_mount_launcher_template.py uses RedFaction.json as a byte-for-byte round-trip fixture, test_gameres_mirror.py pins gameres.h to stage-fleetres.py, and test_fleetres_staging.py checks the -reg entry. Multiplayer is unaffected (resolution is client-local, no anti-cheat). Dash Faction changes the launch path and is Win7+ only.
titles.hw_check: On .145 (XP, DAEMON Tools; RF needs disc 2 visible and has no copy protection), after the hive fix: REGREAD HKCU SOFTWARE\Volition\Red Faction should show Resolution Width 1920 and Height 1080. EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\RedFaction" "Play Red Faction.bat"; SCREENSHOT 0 should be 1920x1080 (today it is 640x480). Start a mission (NEW) and screenshot the HUD. Repeat at 1024x768 for comparison. The menu is mouse-driven and keyboard navigation is not established. To confirm the vendor list: LAUNCH RedFaction.exe, open Setup > Video (a Win32 property sheet, so UICLICK works), press Detect Available Cards and screenshot the list; expect 1280x1024 as the maximum.
titles.verifier_notes: HKCU root confirmed independently, including the base-path builder and the absence of an HKLM fallback. Changes: (1) the surveyor's fix_source omitted the discmount spec, which is what actually generates the shipped launcher, so the proposed stage-fleetres.py edit alone would change nothing; (2) the strings.tbl annotation is not evidence, because the same comment sits above #998 'Name cannot be blank.' and #999 'Invalid Name'; (3) the index getter 0x4b1650 is dead code too; (4) the HUD is width-keyed, which also breaks 1280x960 (FR_W43 on the LCDs), and FLEETRES -cap cannot supply the 4:3 clamp on .123/.240; (5) Dash Faction's Win7+ floor is confirmed from its README; (6) added dgVoodoo 2.87 from the share as a .195-only option. Version: the in-game 'Version 1.00' comes from an unwritten BSS global (0x7d9738), so it neither confirms nor refutes 1.20.

titles.title: Tribes2
titles.engine: Torque/V12 - Tribes 2 v25034.005 (2004 FilePlanet release) + TribesNext RC2a (GameData\Tribes2.exe 4,419,584 B, 2013-03-18); OpenGL by default
titles.launch_sets: Not 1080p: the game starts at 800x600, and there is no resolution mechanism at all. The tree has no FLEETRES.EXE or .BAT, both launchers call none, gameres.h has no rule, and notes.txt says this is deliberate. scripts/clientDefaults.cs sets no $pref::Video::resolution, so the first run uses the engine default 800x600x16 (0x5611f9). On first device activation the card profile (GeForce.cs / Radeon.cs) sets '800 600 32', which is then exported to prefs\ClientPrefs.cs and used from then on. The title has never run on an LCD box. I checked both GameData\base\prefs and GameData\Classic\prefs on .123, .145, .195 and .240 (the surveyor checked only base): no ClientPrefs.cs and no console log anywhere, and the compat DB is 'untested' everywhere. The engine exports ClientPrefs.cs at device activation, so this absence means it never got that far.
titles.menu_source: The list comes from the driver. The Options > Video popup, OP_ResMenu::init in base\scripts.vl2 scripts/OptionsDlg.cs (lines 746-771), adds every getResolutionList(device) entry when fullscreen; only windowed mode drops modes at or above the desktop. The Classic mod's zz_Classic_client_v1.vl2 overloads nothing video-related. The engine's OpenGL list (0x563180) comes from EnumDisplaySettingsA and keeps w>=640, h>=480, bpp 16 or 32, and bpp equal to the desktop unless depth switching is allowed. There is no maximum and no aspect test. $pref::Video::clipHigh (above 1152x864) is set only for NVIDIA 'RIVA TNT/' in CardProfiles.cs. addOSCardProfile carries no ClipHigh column.
titles.evidence: Surveyor's: .claude/evidence-1080p/g6-farcry-bf1942-maxpayne-redfaction-tribes2-r6/tribes2_resolution_list_disasm.txt; staged scripts.vl2, console_start.cs, CardProfiles.cs, GeForce.cs, Radeon.cs, notes.txt and both Play*.bat under /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/Tribes2/. Reviewer: .claude/evidence-1080p/review-g6/tribes2_reviewer_disasm.txt covers the activation order (0x563513-0x5635b7), the profiler's defaults check and export, the console_start.cs lines 101/270-274/425-428/453-457/1017/1164, and the list builder. Also my DIRLIST of base\prefs and Classic\prefs on the four LCD boxes, and a case-insensitive search showing no autoexec.cs or ClientPrefs.cs anywhere in the tree or its .vl2 packages.
titles.fix: No change is needed for the menu. To make the game start at the panel mode without a human, use the engine's own override hook instead of editing ClientPrefs.cs. Stage FLEETRES.EXE/.BAT into Tribes2. In both launchers, after `call FLEETRES.BAT` and before start, write GameData\base\autoexec.cs fresh at every launch, e.g. `> "%~dp0GameData\base\autoexec.cs" echo $pref::Video::resolution = "%FR_W% %FR_H% 32";`, and delete any autoexec.cs.dso. console_start.cs execs autoexec.cs at line 457, after exec($clientprefs) at 427 and before createCanvas at 1164; its own comment reads 'load autoexec again to override video settings/window creation'. The nocalls flag still runs assignments. This avoids three problems with the surveyor's ClientPrefs.cs route: -setline fails on a missing file; the engine rewrites ClientPrefs.cs at device activation and at exit; and exec searches Classic before base, so an engine-written Classic\prefs\ClientPrefs.cs would shadow a launcher-edited base\prefs copy. The surveyor's first-run worry is unfounded for the mode actually set. Activation reads w/h/bpp from the pref before calling the card profiler (0x56356b) and passes those same values to setScreenMode (0x5635a4). The profile's '800 600 32' only lands in the variable and the export, and the autoexec write re-asserts the mode at the next start. Do not set $DisableSystemProfiling: it skips the whole profiler, including the per-card workaround flags. A sync-time twin would need a new GR_OP_CFG body in gameres.h, mirrored in stage-fleetres.py.
titles.fix_source: FLEETRES.EXE/.BAT from provisioning/fleetres (not yet in this tree) plus a new scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py entry. These launchers are not disc-mount launchers, so patch_launcher can anchor on the start line. Nothing to download.
titles.fix_risk: Low. autoexec.cs is a file the engine never writes, and a launcher-owned mode overriding an in-game choice at the next start is the fleet-wide FLEETRES pattern. Must be checked on the box: that exec("autoexec.cs") resolves to GameData\base\autoexec.cs under -mod Classic (otherwise use Classic\autoexec.cs), and that OpenGL at 1920x1080 works on these drivers at all, since the game has never run on any fleet box. Multiplayer is unaffected: resolution is client-local and TribesNext auth is separate.
titles.hw_check: On .145 or .123, when idle: EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\Tribes2" "Play Tribes 2 Solo and LAN.bat"; on XP, SCREENSHOT should show 800x600 today. Open Options > Video > Resolution popup and screenshot the list, which should include '1920 1080'. It is a Torque GUI; if clicks do not land, open the console with UIKEY TILDE and type echo(getResolutionList($pref::Video::displayDevice)); then screenshot the console. After quitting, DIRLIST both GameData\base\prefs and GameData\Classic\prefs to learn which one the engine writes, then DOWNLOAD that ClientPrefs.cs. It should carry $pref::Video::defaultsVendor/defaultsRenderer, which proves device activation. With the autoexec.cs fix in place, the second SCREENSHOT should be 1920x1080.
titles.verifier_notes: Menu verdict confirmed: I re-derived the list builder and OP_ResMenu::init and checked that the Classic overloads do not touch video. Changes: (1) the 'never run' claim was based only on base\prefs; I also checked Classic\prefs and GameData and it holds; (2) the proposed fix is replaced by the engine's autoexec.cs override hook, because the ClientPrefs.cs route has a shadowing and missing-file failure mode; (3) the disassembly shows the first-run card profile does not change the first mode actually set, so a second launch should not be needed; (4) warned against $DisableSystemProfiling.

titles.title: RainbowSix
titles.engine: Red Storm 'Sherman' engine - Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six (1998), GOG build, readme v1.04 (RainbowSix.exe md5 c92073e4c74c2c36ef1a644f913814a5, identical to the share's source copy); DirectDraw + Direct3D immediate mode, software renderer selectable via DevicePicker.exe
titles.launch_sets: 640x480 fullscreen on the 1080p LCDs. There is no FLEETRES in the tree and no gameres.h rule, and the launcher documents that on purpose. install.reg sets FullScreen=1 and SoftwareOnly=0 but no VideoResolution, so the compiled default '640x480' applies. Measured 2026-09-01 on .123: the main menu rendered at 640x480 (ddraw). .123's HKLM now holds VideoResolution='640x480', written by the game; .145, .195 and .240 have no value. The exe imports RegCreateKeyExA and not RegOpenKeyEx, and all 8 call sites use HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE (0x80000002), so HKLM is the right hive. DevicePicker.exe offers only the device and software-renderer choice, no resolution.
titles.menu_source: The list is hardcoded. Options > VIDEO > RESOLUTION is a radio set from the pointer table at 0x8a53a0: '320x240 LOW', '640x480 MED', '800x600 HIGH'. Beyond the menu, the renderer's DirectDraw mode callback (0x497dd0, registered at 0x46ea5e) drops every mode with dwWidth > 1024 or dwHeight > 768 and keeps at most 50. VideoResolution is parsed generically at 0x40e5e0, then looked up exactly in that capped list (0x46ff7c). The surveyor's 'otherwise it fails' is overstated. A miss raises 'Unable to find a display mode to match request' inside the caller's own try-frame, and execution continues into PickDriverAndMode (0x470be0) with the requested size. The outcome is unverified; a GOG forum report says VideoResolution=1920x1080 ends up at 1024x768.
titles.evidence: Surveyor's: .claude/evidence-1080p/g6-farcry-bf1942-maxpayne-redfaction-tribes2-r6/{rainbowsix_1024x768_cap_disasm.txt, registry_readback_lcd_boxes.json, r6_123_main_menu_2026-09-01.png}; staged Play Rainbow Six.bat and install.reg. Reviewer: .claude/evidence-1080p/review-g6/rainbowsix_reviewer_notes.txt covers the callback, the labels, the 8 HKLM sites and DevicePicker. My read-only runs of the surveyor's exact recipe on the four LCD boxes are in .claude/evidence-1080p/review-g6/fleetres_cmd_cap1024x768_{123,145,195,240}.txt and fleetres_info_cap1024x768_*.txt. .claude/evidence-1080p/review-g6/dgvoodoo_2_87_subsystems.txt covers dgVoodoo. Web background: PCGW community file 3438 'Widescreen & FOV Fix' needs ThirteenAG's Ultimate ASI Loader as ddraw.dll.
titles.fix: Stock 1.04 has no route to a 1080p entry in any menu, and its renderer drops every mode above 1024x768. The surveyor's 1024x768 recipe is WRONG on half the LCDs. `call FLEETRES.BAT -cap 1024 768` then `%FR_W43%x%FR_H43%` gives 1024x768 on .145 and .195 but 640x480 on .123 and .240, measured with FLEETRES -cmd. On those two boxes -cap re-targets to their 16:9 848x480 mode first, and FR_W43 is the largest 4:3 mode inside that. Correct recipe: stage FLEETRES.EXE/.BAT; in 'Play Rainbow Six.bat' run `call FLEETRES.BAT` with no cap; then clamp in the batch file: set R6RES=%FR_W43%x%FR_H43%, and if FR_W43 is greater than 1024 set R6RES=1024x768. Then run FLEETRES.EXE -reg HKLM "SOFTWARE\Red Storm Entertainment\Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six" VideoResolution sz %R6RES%. This gives 1024x768 on all four LCDs and on .133, 1024x768 on .124 and .143, and 800x600 on .171. Do NOT add an uncapped gameres.h %W43%x%H43% rule: that is 1280x960 on the LCDs, outside the game's list. A sync-time rule needs a capped token first. Beyond 4:3, both options are .195-only: (a) the PCGW Widescreen & FOV Fix v1.1 plus the Ultimate ASI Loader as ddraw.dll, not on the share, with no documented XP build (the 2020 loader in Max_Payne_Fixes.zip is subsystem 6.0); (b) dgVoodoo 2.87, on the share, whose x86 DDraw/D3DImm are subsystem 6.0 and can force a higher internal render resolution. Neither adds a 1080p menu entry.
titles.fix_source: For 1024x768: FLEETRES from provisioning/fleetres plus a scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py entry (not a mount launcher, so patch_launcher can anchor on `cd /d`). gameres.h would need a capped token. For .195 only: \\192.168.1.122\files\Files\Game Updates\dgVoodoo2_87.zip (on the share); community.pcgamingwiki.com/files/file/3438 and github.com/ThirteenAG/Ultimate-ASI-Loader (would need downloading).
titles.fix_risk: The clamp is low risk. Unverified: whether the 640x480 shell and planning screens switch cleanly to a 1024x768 mission, and that DirectDraw lists 1024x768 at the game's bpp on Win7 (.195). R6 has only been run on .123. The ASI route per its notes needs the exe renamed on Win10 (AcGenral shim) and still stops at 50 enumerated modes. The ASI and dgVoodoo routes change the load path, are Win7-only, and have unknown HUD and stretch behaviour. Multiplayer (-server/-client) is resolution-independent and the game has no anti-cheat.
titles.hw_check: On .145 or .123, when idle: REGREAD HKLM "SOFTWARE\Red Storm Entertainment\Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six" and note VideoResolution. EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\RainbowSix" "Play Rainbow Six.bat", let intro.smk finish (ESC quits the game), then SCREENSHOT 0 the 640x480 main menu (XP; 16-bit DirectDraw captures). Options > VIDEO > RESOLUTION should show only 320x240 LOW / 640x480 MED / 800x600 HIGH. The shell draws its own cursor and keyboard navigation is not established, so it may need a human once. For the clamp: after the launcher runs, REGREAD should show VideoResolution=1024x768; start a mission, then run SCREENSHOT and DISPLAYCFG get in the mission (expect 1024x768). Test .123 or .240 specifically, since those are the boxes where the -cap recipe fails.
titles.verifier_notes: Menu verdict, the 1024x768 cap and the HKLM hive are confirmed; I also checked all 8 registry sites and DevicePicker. REFUTED the proposed fix: the surveyor's '-cap 1024 768 + FR_W43' gives 640x480 on .123 and .240 (read-only FLEETRES -cmd on all four LCD boxes); replaced it with a batch-level clamp. Softened 'otherwise it fails': the miss is caught locally and execution continues into PickDriverAndMode, outcome unverified. Added dgVoodoo 2.87, which IS on the share, as a .195-only option, and warned against an uncapped gameres rule.
